title: Normalization of an explicitly constructed positive chart recursion
statement: Fix a finite purity setting P [def-pur-conventions], a k-scheme T, its signed finite coefficient sheaves [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data] and normalized signed products [def-pur-finite-signed-twist-products]. Given an ordinary sheaf isomorphism e1 from the first signed sheaf to the coefficient unit, construct e0 by the coefficient realization unit/counit and the constant-module unit comparison [def-pur-proetale-constant-module-unit] and define e(n+2) as the inverse signed product in degrees n+1 and 1 followed by e(n+1) tensor e1 and the left unitor. For every natural degree d, site object V, coherent signed frame b, and ordinary representatives x1 and x of b(1) and b(d), if e1 sends x1 to coefficient one, the explicitly recursive chart e(d) sends x to coefficient one. This is an assertion about the constructed recursion, with no existence or uniqueness assertion.

source.place: Step 2, compatibility with the invertible twist by associativity of derived tensor; expanded Step 8 of def-pur-finite-positive-root-charts.

proof.text: At zero the realization unit/counit and the constant module unit comparison take the frame basis one to the coefficient-one section. At one the assertion is precisely the given hypothesis on e1.

Induct on positive powers. Realization identifies ordinary and intrinsic section modules. Lift the degree n+1 frame vector to an ordinary section. The normalized signed product in degrees n+1 and 1 takes its pure tensor with x1 to the degree n+2 frame vector, by the positive frame axiom. Since realization and the product are injective, its inverse takes x to that pure tensor. Apply the induction hypothesis and the hypothesis on e1. Naturality of the ordinary tensor and the unit unitor take the tensor of the two coefficient-one sections to coefficient one.

proof_origin.place: Explicit ordinary-sheaf realization of the positive-power construction in Step 2.

theorem finiteTensorOrdinaryChartRecursion_normalized (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [T.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (e₁ : P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T 1 ≅
      𝟙_ (Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient)))
    (d : ℕ) (V : T.ProEt) (b : P.FiniteTensorFrame T V)
    (x₁ : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T 1).obj.obj (Opposite.op V))
    (x : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T d).obj.obj (Opposite.op V))
    (hx₁ : HEq (P.finiteTensorSection T 1 V x₁) (P.finiteTensorFrameBasis T V b 1))
    (he₁ : e₁.hom.hom.app (Opposite.op V) x₁ =
      (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (sheafToPresheaf (ProEt.topology T)
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))).app (Opposite.op V) (1 : P.Coefficient))
    (hx : HEq (P.finiteTensorSection T d V x) (P.finiteTensorFrameBasis T V b d)) :
    (P.finiteTensorOrdinaryChartRecursion T e₁ d).hom.hom.app (Opposite.op V) x =
      (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (sheafToPresheaf (ProEt.topology T)
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))).app (Opposite.op V) (1 : P.Coefficient)
